# PermissionDiff 0.2.0

A feature release. All additions are backward compatible: existing configs, snapshots, and case
fingerprints are unchanged, and security verdicts stay deterministic.

## Added

- **Persistent worker execution (default).** The authorizer is imported once in a long-lived worker
  and cases stream over a line-delimited protocol — roughly an order of magnitude faster on large
  corpora. Any crash or timeout kills and re-spawns the worker so one bad case cannot corrupt later
  cases, and output stays byte-identical for deterministic authorizers. Set
  `execution.worker: process_per_case` to restore a fresh interpreter per case.
- **Git-aware diffing.** `permissiondiff diff --git-ref REF` evaluates the baseline authorizer as it
  existed at a git ref, checked out into a temporary auto-removed worktree — no snapshot file needed.
  `--baseline` and `--git-ref` are mutually exclusive.
- **Least-privilege mining.** `permissiondiff mine` reports the authorizer's effective grant surface
  and flags broad grants (cross-tenant or non-owner) for review.
- **Policy-engine adapter toolkit.** `permissiondiff.adapters` (`from_boolean`, `from_decision`,
  `http_authorizer`) wraps an external policy engine as the authorizer. Runnable example adapters for
  OPA, OpenFGA, Auth0 FGA, Cedar, and SpiceDB ship under `examples/adapters/`.
- **Delegation checks.** A subject may declare `delegated_by: [id, ...]`; a delegated principal
  allowed where any delegator is denied (on the identical case) is a critical privilege-escalation
  finding. `delegated_by` is serialized only when present, so existing fingerprints/snapshots are
  unchanged.

## Not included (still deferred)

Live agent/MCP tool-call (shadow) interception remains out of scope — it requires a runtime, which
is intentionally outside v0's pure-decision-function boundary. This release ships the deterministic,
offline core of the delegation model instead.

## Install

```bash
pip install permissiondiff==0.2.0
```

Python 3.12, 3.13, and 3.14 are supported.

## Security note (unchanged)

PermissionDiff evaluates trusted Python authorization code in a timeout-controlled subprocess, which
provides fault isolation, not a hostile-code security sandbox. Adapters make read-only decision
calls; point them at a non-production policy instance. Run in an isolated development or CI
environment, never against production data or code with side effects.

See the [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/abishekgiri/permissiondiff/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) for
details.
